name: Harris Teeter Perishable Distribution Center Indian Trail NC

fieldNotes.campusSplit: 6001 W Hwy 74 is ONE shared Harris Teeter DC campus holding a refrigerated/perishable section and a dry grocery section in a single connected mega-structure, plus a separate fleet/fuel support building near the entrance. This audit covers the PERISHABLE (refrigerated) portion: the bright white high-albedo cool-roof NW half of the main building and its NE/NW dock face and adjacent reefer drop yard. The grey-roof SE half is the dry grocery DC (covered by sister agent). Perimeter/dock/drop geofences are drawn around the perishable section only; the truck gate, access drive and guard shack are shared by the whole campus.
fieldNotes.truckGate: Controlled inner gate at the throat where the ~250m private access drive opens into the yard. Satellite z21 shows a guard booth beside the lane with a yellow barrier arm and a channelizing island; Street View pano LewhTCax-ZFpoxel2VkUmQ (2025-11) shows the gatehouse, STOP sign, pedestrian-crossing caution sign, lane markings and chain-link perimeter fencing.
fieldNotes.guardShack: Staffed booth (~1-2 vehicle footprint, multi-window) sitting beside the truck lane at the inner gate, with STOP/check-in signage. Clearly a manned guard shack, not the main building.
fieldNotes.fastLaneOpportunity: Gate throat opens into a very wide multi-lane paved apron with substantial unused width beside the single guarded lane; physical room to add an express/bypass lane.
fieldNotes.postGateStaging: Large deep paved yard inside the gate before the dock doors; trucks visibly staged there in Street View.
fieldNotes.drivewayLong: Approach yard easily holds 3+ trucks; plus the ~250m tree-lined private drive from US-74 to the gate gives deep buffering.
fieldNotes.backupSensitive: Long private drive plus deep internal yard means a gate queue would not spill onto US-74; not backup-sensitive.
fieldNotes.dockDoorCount: ~38 doors estimated along the perishable building's NE and NW faces from z18/z19 imagery (reefer trailers backed in); band 25-50. Exact count uncertain where the perishable dock line transitions into the grocery section.
fieldNotes.dropArea: Dedicated reefer trailer drop/parking lot NE of the perishable docks; ~60 trailers visible, capacity ~90; band 25-50.
fieldNotes.shipRcvSeparate: Perishable building works from a single continuous dock bank (NE/NW face); shipping and receiving not on physically separate building faces, so false. Some uncertainty given the connected grocery docks.
fieldNotes.urbanRural: Indian Trail is on the southeast fringe of the Charlotte metro. Site itself is wooded edge-of-town with retention ponds and a railroad on the west edge; commercial/retail strip across US-74 to the NE and a residential subdivision to the SE. Judged Rural per rubric tie-break (small-town/edge-of-town industrial over Urban).
fieldNotes.multipleFacilities: Campus: connected perishable+grocery mega-DC, a separate fleet/fuel/maintenance building near the entrance, and a third large building in the SW corner.
fieldNotes.railServed: A rail line runs along the western edge of the property but no spur visibly enters the buildings; treated as not rail-served.
fieldNotes.scale: No truck scale/weigh pad visible in the truck path at the gate or in the yard.
fieldNotes.coords: Pinned to the perishable building centroid (white-roof NW section), confirmed via satellite z16-z21 and Street View; the supplied campus coords (35.065177, -80.645931) landed near the shared entrance/parking area, not the perishable building.
